title: Analysis of bilateral muscle coordination for characterizing neuromuscular function in postural control
author: Promsri

steps.title: Recruit participants and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Enroll 25 physically active young adults (14 M, 11 F; age 25.6 ± 4.0 yr, weight 71.0 ± 11.5 kg, height 175.0 ± 8.3 cm, BMI 23.1 ± 2.7 kg/m², activity 8.4 ± 5.1 h/week) who report no neurological or musculoskeletal problems and no balance‑specific training for ≥6 months; obtain written informed consent after ethical approval (University of Innsbruck, Declaration of Helsinki).

steps.title: Familiarization on balance boards
steps.instruction: Give each participant a 15‑second familiarization trial on each balance board with no instruction or feedback.

steps.title: Perform balancing trials
steps.instruction: Randomly conduct an 80‑second barefoot bipedal balancing trial on each support surface (stable and two unstable boards).

steps.title: Standardize foot placement
steps.instruction: Place two marked points on the base of each 2nd metatarsal bone over a horizontal line taped on the floor for the stable‑surface trial or over the board’s horizontal diameter for unstable trials; align the insides of the feet (medial borders of the first metatarsal distal ends) to an inter‑feet distance equal to 15 % of the participant’s bi‑acromial diameter.

steps.title: Standardize board position
steps.instruction: Center each balance board over a reticle crossline marked on the floor; align the board’s taped anteroposterior and mediolateral diameters with the crossed lines so that the fulcrum position is identical for all participants and trials.

steps.title: Maintain visual and postural conditions
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to look straight ahead at a 10‑cm diameter red circle placed at eye level on a wall ~5 m away, stand still for stable trials, avoid extraneous movements (e.g., scratching, head rotation), keep the board horizontal for unstable trials, and rest 1–3 minutes (sitting or standing) between trials (no standing on the board).

steps.title: Preprocess EMG signals
steps.instruction: Filter each EMG channel with a 2nd‑order band‑pass Butterworth filter (20–500 Hz), rectify, then smooth with a 3rd‑order zero‑phase 10‑Hz low‑pass Butterworth filter; down‑sample to 250 Hz; select the middle 60 s (15 000 points) of data; split this segment into ten 6‑second subsets (1 500 points each).

steps.title: Compute EMG cross‑correlation
steps.instruction: For each 6‑second subset, apply Matlab™ function XCORR to obtain the normalized cross‑correlation; record the peak correlation coefficient |r| and its time delay τ; classify |r| as small (0.1–0.3), moderate (0.3–0.5), or large (0.5–1.0).

steps.title: Average correlation per participant
steps.instruction: Average the |r| values across all ten subsets for each participant; if statistical comparison is required, transform the averaged |r| using Fisher’s r‑to‑z conversion.

steps.title: Prepare data for pattern analysis
steps.instruction: Average the cross‑correlation coefficients of each muscle across subsets, z‑score normalize them, and concatenate the results for all participants and conditions into a single spreadsheet (75 rows = 25 participants × 3 balance conditions; 7 columns = 7 muscles).

steps.title: Perform principal component analysis
steps.instruction: Run Matlab™ function pca on the prepared dataset to obtain eigenvectors (PCk), eigenvalues (EVk), and scores for every trial.

steps.title: Compare pattern contributions
steps.instruction: Calculate relative explained variances (rVARk) from the PCA scores for each condition; compare rVARk across conditions to assess differences in bilateral EMG‑EMG correlation patterns.
